content.question_text: What is the key difference between a static field and an instance field?

core_requirements: A static field is not present in individual objects — there is only one single copy of it shared among all instances of the class.
An instance field exists once per object — every object has its own copy.
acceptable_variations: Static field belongs to the class; instance field belongs to each object.

content.question_text: Does a static field exist even when there are no objects of the class instantiated? Explain.

core_requirements: Yes — a static field belongs to the class itself, not to any individual object.
Even if there are no instances of the class, the static field is still present in memory.
acceptable_variations: Static fields exist at class level, independent of any object creation.

content.question_text: What is a static constant, and how does it differ from a static variable?

core_requirements: A static constant is a static field declared with the final modifier, meaning its value can never be changed after initialization.
Static variables are rare and can be modified; static constants are more common and are fixed values shared across all instances.
acceptable_variations: static final = constant shared by all; static alone = shared variable that can change.

content.question_text: Why is it acceptable to make a static constant public, even though instance fields should normally be private?

core_requirements: Because the constant is declared as final, it cannot be reassigned or modified by outside code.
There is no risk of encapsulation being broken since the value is fixed.
acceptable_variations: public final = safe to expose because nobody can change it.

content.question_text: What is a static method, and what makes it different from a regular instance method?

core_requirements: A static method does not operate on objects — it has no implicit parameter (no 'this').
A regular instance method operates on the object it is invoked on and has access to the object's instance fields.
acceptable_variations: Static method = no 'this', no instance fields accessible. Instance method = operates on an object.

content.question_text: What are the two situations where you should use a static method?

core_requirements: When a method doesn't need to access the object state because all needed parameters are supplied as explicit parameters (e.g. Math.pow).
When a method only needs to access static fields of the class (e.g. Employee.advanceId).
acceptable_variations: No object state needed, or only static fields needed.

content.question_text: How do you call a static method, and why is calling it via an object reference discouraged?

core_requirements: You call a static method by supplying the class name (e.g. Employee.advanceId()).
Calling it via an object reference (e.g. harry.advanceId()) is legal but confusing, because the method doesn't look at the object at all — it suggests a relationship to the object that doesn't exist.
acceptable_variations: Use ClassName.method() — calling via object is misleading since the object is ignored.

content.question_text: What is a factory method, and which kind of method is it?

core_requirements: A factory method is a static method that constructs and returns objects instead of using a constructor directly.
Examples include LocalDate.now() and LocalDate.of(), and NumberFormat.getCurrencyInstance().
acceptable_variations: Factory method = static method that creates and returns objects.

content.question_text: What are the three reasons to prefer a factory method over a constructor?

core_requirements: You can give factory methods meaningful names (constructors must always have the same name as the class).
Factory methods can return objects of a subclass type — constructors always return the exact type of the class.
Factory methods can return a shared existing instance rather than always constructing a new object.
acceptable_variations: Named methods, variable return type, object sharing/reuse.

content.question_text: Why was the main method traditionally declared as static?

core_requirements: When a program starts, there are no objects yet.
The main method must be callable without any existing object, so it must be static.
acceptable_variations: No objects exist at program startup, so main must be static to be called without one.

content.question_text: As of Java 25, what are the rules that determine which main method is chosen when there is more than one?

core_requirements: Static main methods are preferred over instance main methods.
Methods with a String[] parameter are preferred over those with no parameters.
Private main methods are not considered.
If main is not static, the class must have a non-private no-argument constructor — the launcher constructs an instance and invokes main on it.
acceptable_variations: Any correct rephrasing of the four rules from the book.

content.question_text: What is a compact compilation unit in Java 25, and what does it implicitly create?

core_requirements: A compact compilation unit is a source file that contains method declarations outside of any class.
It implicitly declares a class whose name is derived from the source file name, and top-level variables and methods become instance fields and methods of that class.
acceptable_variations: Source file with methods outside a class — Java implicitly wraps them in a class named after the file.
